outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin reports Galapagos birds and reptiles, South American fossils, animal size and vegetation, the former Pampas horse, and extinction; he asks Lyell about species.

observations.description: Darwin’s question about Lyell’s late shell work is not an identifiable response to incoming 343 or 376, whose surviving subjects do not supply that wording; the antecedent remains outside the packet.

evidence.quote: Has your late work at shells startled you about the existence of species?

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 343 concerns coral islands and an invitation to London; it does not supply the shell-work prompt. Incoming 376 discusses Crag shells but is a travel and report letter without an explicit connection to this question; a nearer or missing Lyell letter remains possible.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin answers a Lyell query about the geographic limits and distribution of Pacific coral islands, discusses the Corallian Sea and volcanic bands, and adds a Tuesday-night continuation.

observations.description: The editorial summary identifies a Lyell query about the northern and southern limits of Pacific coral islands, and the body answers it, but that initiating Lyell text is not in this packet. Incoming 343 and 376 do not contain that distinctive query.

evidence.quote: I cannot say what are the southern or northern limits of true coral islands in Pacific

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 343 discusses Darwin’s coral lesson but not Pacific limits; incoming 376 concerns Scandinavian geology and Crag shells. The exact Lyell prompt is missing and must be obtained externally.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Lyell for the Elements, reports his Glen Roy expedition and work, discusses the Athenaeum, British Association, entomology, barometric readings and Scottish lake heights, and comments on FitzRoy.

observations.description: The opening establishes that Darwin is responding to Lyell’s note and book, but the surviving incoming 425 is dated later and is itself a response to this letter; 424 is therefore an outgoing antecedent rather than a response to 425.

evidence.quote: Very many thanks for the present of your elements, which I received, (& I believe the very first copy distributed) together with your note.

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 343 and 376 predate 424 but contain no Elements-receipt or Glen Roy prompt matching this full response. Incoming 425 explicitly says it is answering a Darwin letter, supporting 424 as its antecedent.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Lyell’s long letter about the Prescott/Newfoundland document, the Elements, geological theory, Glen Roy, the British Association, Owen, Charlesworth and his own species notebooks.

observations.description: Darwin explicitly answers the long surviving Lyell letter 425, beginning with gratitude for its length and then addressing its book, Kinnordy invitation, geological discussion and British Association material. The response is to 425 as a whole, with no assumption that its two dated sections were received simultaneously. The Prescott document mentioned in 428 is an unlocated or intervening enclosure: 425 does not contain it.

evidence.quote: I was astonished & delighted at your gloriously long letter
I assure you my father is quite enthusiastic about your journal
My father has been more and more taken up and delighted with your journal, and begged me this morning to invite you to come here any day this or the next month
pray give my best thanks to Mr Lyell, for his very kind invitation
in this country no importance is attached to any body of men who do not make occasional demonstrations of their strength in public meetings
I am glad to hear what a favourable report you give of the British association

observations.description: The Prescott/Newfoundland document is discussed by Darwin in 428, but it is absent from 425 and must not be attributed to that letter; an intervening or missing Lyell communication or enclosure is needed.

evidence.quote: it is about that unfortunate letter of Governor Prescott

observations.description: The retained body is dated by editorial/XML material as 14 September while its header says Friday night September 13th; the response link is to the complete 425 record, whose own 6 and 8 September sections remain a multi-date source.

evidence.quote: I only received one letter from you at Newcastle

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 343 and 376 are earlier but do not contain the distinctive long-letter and Prescott/Newfoundland material.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin announces his engagement to Emma Wedgwood, expresses gratitude for Lyell’s friendship, and says he will be in town the following week.

observations.description: This is a personal announcement to Lyell with no surviving Lyell letter in the packet explicitly prompting it; topic or catalogue adjacency cannot identify an antecedent.

evidence.quote: I write because, I cannot avoid wishing to be the first person to tell Mrs Lyell and yourself

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 425 is too early and has no engagement prompt; the initiating context may have been oral or in a missing letter.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin sends his completed Glen Roy paper, discusses Lyell’s shell information and MacLaren’s alluvium chapters, and comments on erratic boulders and Lochaber.

observations.description: Darwin says he used Lyell’s information about decaying shells in a note to the Glen Roy paper. This may refer to 425’s discussion of shell-less Swedish deposits, but the wording does not identify 425 uniquely and an intervening Lyell note is not supplied; retain as candidate-only.

evidence.quote: Your information about the decaying shells, I have introduced in a note as you sent it me, in inverted commas

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-425 p8 discusses deposits destitute of shells and is the nearest surviving topical candidate, but the exact phrase “decaying shells” and intervening time leave an unlocated Lyell note possible.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin discusses his illness, the Coral reefs manuscript and revisions, coral depth and classification, and Ehrenberg’s observations.

observations.description: Darwin thanks Lyell for a kind note and then answers or updates him on coral-research matters, but no incoming Lyell record in this packet supplies that note.

evidence.quote: Many thanks for your kind note.

alternative_candidates_considered: No assigned incoming record near February 1840 contains the illness or manuscript note; the exact Lyell communication is needed.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin answers geological questions about Chiloé, erratic boulders, perched rocks on the Jura, Agassiz and the limits of negative evidence.

observations.description: The editorial summary says this letter answers several Lyell queries, but the queried text is not among the five incoming records; the body itself identifies the answers as being written while reading Lyell’s material.

evidence.quote: I will write down my answers as I read Chiloe is 100 miles long.

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 604 is from July 1841 and cannot be the missing February–April query; no safe incoming record in this packet supplies Lyell’s Chiloé/Jura questions.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin continues a discussion of Agassiz and Lyell’s Jura erratic theory, addressing ice, glaciers, subsidence and the Pentlands.

observations.description: This bounded March memorandum continues discussion of Lyell’s manuscript, but no corresponding Lyell incoming text is retained. Theological and geological topic overlap with other Darwin letters cannot identify a prompt.

evidence.quote: I find I do not know enough of case to enter in your difficulty about subsidence.

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-590 and 595 concern related Jura material but are both Darwin-to-Lyell records, not incoming prompts; the underlying Lyell manuscript remains external.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin defends his marine-beach interpretation of Glen Roy against a glacier explanation and asks Lyell to consider specific geological difficulties.

observations.description: Darwin explicitly says he has received Lyell’s note, but that note is not assigned among the incoming records; it cannot be reconstructed from the editorial discussion alone.

evidence.quote: I have just received your note

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 604 is months later and unrelated; the March Lyell note that prompted this letter is unlocated.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin works through Lyell’s extract and Agassiz’s glacier theory, discusses Jura boulders, Glen Roy, Niagara and his South American boulder paper.

observations.description: Darwin’s opening attributes the immediate questions to Lyell’s extract, but the extract and its enclosing Lyell communication are not in the packet.

evidence.quote: Your extract has set me puzzling me very much

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-594 is an earlier Darwin letter that mentions a Lyell note, not the missing Lyell extract; no incoming record identifies this prompt.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin responds to Lyell’s forwarded letter about Silurian coral limestone, coral-reef classification and mapping, Bermuda, health, and the Lyells’ imminent American trip.

observations.description: Darwin says Lyell’s letter was forwarded to him, but that incoming letter is absent from the packet. The later incoming 604 is a reply to 602 and cannot serve as its prompt.

evidence.quote: Your letter was forwarded me here.

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 604 follows and answers this letter but is not the antecedent; the forwarded Lyell letter itself must be obtained externally.

outgoing_reviews.summary: A date-uncertain memorandum reconsidering how much subsidence the coral-reef theory requires, distinguishing groups of islands from large tracts of land.

observations.description: The editorial note says this memorandum was likely written after Lyell returned from America and discussed Coral reefs with Darwin, but no such Lyell discussion or letter is retained. The broad September–December date range remains held as uncertain.

evidence.quote: Considering the probability of subsidence in the middle of the great oceans being very slow

alternative_candidates_considered: The editorially described oral discussion and Lyell’s returned copy of Coral reefs are not preserved here; no incoming record can be promoted by topic overlap.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin discusses coral species and dead reefs, then records Geological Society Council events involving Charlesworth, Lonsdale, Murchison and Agassiz’s Glen Roy observations.

observations.description: This two-date letter contains Darwin’s own report of Council events and geological discussions, but no surviving Lyell letter is explicitly acknowledged as its prompt.

evidence.quote: Once again thank you for your letter.— Friday morning

alternative_candidates_considered: The letter thanked is not among the five incoming records; 653 is a later Darwin-to-Lyell follow-up and cannot be treated as an incoming prompt.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin warns Lyell that the Charlesworth solicitor’s Council letter may have been designed to entrap the Geological Society and asks him to have it reread.

observations.description: The editorial footnote points back to Darwin’s 649 account of the Council controversy, but the immediate Lyell communication that led to this note is absent. Because 649 and 653 are both Darwin-to-Lyell records, 649 cannot be the incoming prompt.

evidence.quote: I have just taken down the controversial pamphlet of Charlsworth

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-649 is a prior outgoing Darwin report, not an incoming Lyell letter; the external Lyell communication or oral exchange remains needed.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin writes about the expected birth, the British Association, Waterhouse, Lonsdale, Kemp’s seeds and his Volcanic islands manuscript.

observations.description: Darwin requests news of Lyell’s activities and reports letters from Waterhouse and Lonsdale, but no incoming Lyell letter in the packet is acknowledged or uniquely identified. The 15-or-22 September alternatives remain unresolved.

evidence.quote: I do not know whether you are still at Kinnordy

alternative_candidates_considered: Incoming 670 is from April 1843 and concerns a Geological Society grant and fossils, not this September exchange; no assigned antecedent is available.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin defends his interpretation of the tosca formation in Uruguay and the Rio Negro, correcting d’Orbigny and explaining the evidence from stratified sections and pumice.

observations.description: The geological argument is presented to Lyell, but no incoming Lyell text in this packet is explicitly answered; the antecedent may be an external letter, manuscript discussion or oral exchange.

evidence.quote: I have been looking over my huge bundle of notes & I find that the proposition that the Tosca was a diluvial mud is monstrous.

alternative_candidates_considered: No incoming record near December 1843 supplies a tosca prompt. The external text or oral discussion is required.

outgoing_reviews.summary: A printed multi-signer memorial to Thomas Spring Rice urging purchase of the Mantell and Hawkins collections for the British Museum; it is a public petition, not a Darwin-to-Lyell letter, and is explicitly held for the period workflow.

observations.description: This record is outside the eligible correspondence set: its metadata is ambiguous/bounded and the text is a public memorial addressed to a government official with multiple signatories, including Darwin and Lyell. It cannot establish a Lyell prompt or a private response pair.

evidence.quote: The Memorial of your Petitioners humbly Showeth,

alternative_candidates_considered: No incoming Lyell prompt can be inferred from a public petition. The original XML hold and multi-sender attribution must remain unchanged.

incoming_reviews.summary: Lyell invites Darwin to the Geological Society and Anniversary dinner, praises his coral and elevation work, and jokes about diluvialist disbelief.

observations.description: No assigned Darwin outgoing letter explicitly answers this invitation or the Anniversary dinner. Darwin 367 later discusses species and fossils without the distinctive meeting invitation; incoming dates are not receipt dates.

evidence.quote: it strikes me as right to tell you, to come up by all means on the 17th. instt

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-367 is the next assigned Darwin record but does not mention the Geological Society invitation; a response may be missing or oral.

incoming_reviews.summary: Lyell writes in two dated sections about Scandinavian granite, German geology, Crag shells and Beck’s identifications, and asks Darwin to support his Crag classification publicly.

observations.description: The surviving Darwin 394 answers a different, editorially identified missing Lyell query about Pacific coral limits. Darwin 367 predates this letter’s September section and does not answer the Beck/Crag request; no direct response is established.

evidence.quote: will you state that you happen to know from correspondence which you have had with me this summer

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-394 contains no Beck/Crag response and its editorial summary identifies another missing query. A Darwin response to this public Crag request is unlocated.

incoming_reviews.summary: Lyell replies in 6 and 8 September sections to Darwin’s Elements and Glen Roy letter, discusses geology, the British Association and species, and includes information on shell-less deposits.

observations.description: Lyell explicitly says he is rereading and answering Darwin’s letter, and the content matches 424’s Elements, Glen Roy, Athenaeum and British Association discussion. This is a response from Lyell to Darwin 424; it does not by itself prove when Darwin received it.

evidence.quote: I must first read your letter again which I answered in a great hurry at Newcastle
I have fully convinced myself, (after some doubting at first) that the shelves are sea-beaches

observations.description: Paragraph 3 begins the explicitly dated September 8 section; the record’s 6 and 8 September sections should remain distinct when evaluating delivery and response order.

evidence.quote: September 8.— Many thanks for the ‘Spectator’ which came this morning.

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-428 is Darwin’s later direct response to this 425 record; 480 may use 425’s shell observations but remains candidate-only because the exact intervening prompt is missing.

incoming_reviews.summary: Lyell regrets missing Darwin before the American trip, describes the loss of their London intercourse, and returns Darwin’s coral charts.

observations.description: Lyell 604 appears to answer Darwin 602’s account of staying in the country and the coral charts, but identity is not confirmed: 602 expected to return on 15 or 16 July and promised another letter if plans changed, while 604 says his father persuaded him to stay. A missing later change-of-plan note may be the actual prompt. Charts and illness establish context rather than a unique direct pair; this remains candidate-only.

evidence.quote: I have no doubt that your father did righly in persuading you to stay
I think we shall return about 15th or 16th
I have told my clerk to send to your house the charts on Coral reefs you kindly lent me
I will think of your suggestion of a neutral tint for such coral-reefs

alternative_candidates_considered: No other incoming Lyell record near July 1841 addresses Darwin’s stay, charts or departure; 602 is the clear antecedent.

incoming_reviews.summary: Lyell reports discussions with Geological Society officers about Darwin’s proposed government publication grant, an upcoming fossil-tree paper, Halstead’s observations and U.S. fossils.

observations.description: Lyell says the officers acted on what Darwin had suggested, but the suggested proposal or Darwin letter is not among the assigned outgoing records; no direct Darwin antecedent can be identified from the packet.

evidence.quote: said all you had suggested

alternative_candidates_considered: DCP-LETT-696 is later and concerns Waterhouse, Lonsdale and seeds; it cannot be the antecedent. The relevant Darwin proposal is external.

proposed_links.reason: Lyell explicitly says he is answering Darwin’s letter, and the Elements, Glen Roy and British Association material matches 424’s body. The two dated sections remain a multi-date source; no receipt date is inferred.

evidence.quote: I must first read your letter again which I answered in a great hurry at Newcastle
Very many thanks for the present of your elements, which I received

As to the Glen Roy case, I saw, in Orust in Sweden, great beds of stratified gravel and sand like those which cover our Scotch hypogene rocks entirely destitute of shells; yet there were beds of shells like those of Uddevalla

proposed_links.reason: Darwin explicitly calls 425 a gloriously long letter and answers its book, Kinnordy invitation, geological and British Association discussions. The Prescott document mentioned in 428 is not in 425 and is treated separately as an unlocated/intervening enclosure. The response is assessed across the complete 425 record while preserving 425’s two dated sections.

evidence.quote: I was astonished & delighted at your gloriously long letter
I assure you my father is quite enthusiastic about your journal
My father has been more and more taken up and delighted with your journal, and begged me this morning to invite you to come here any day this or the next month
pray give my best thanks to Mr Lyell, for his very kind invitation
in this country no importance is attached to any body of men who do not make occasional demonstrations of their strength in public meetings
I am glad to hear what a favourable report you give of the British association

proposed_links.reason: 480 says Darwin incorporated Lyell’s shell information into the Glen Roy paper, and 425 reports shell-less Swedish deposits. The topic is distinctive enough to retain as a candidate, but “decaying shells” does not uniquely identify 425 and an intervening or missing Lyell note remains possible.

evidence.quote: Your information about the decaying shells, I have introduced in a note as you sent it me, in inverted commas
great beds of stratified gravel and sand like those which cover our Scotch hypogene rocks entirely destitute of shells

proposed_links.reason: 604 may answer 602’s account of staying away and the coral charts, but 602 expected to return on 15 or 16 July and promised another letter if plans changed, whereas 604 says his father persuaded him to stay. A missing change-of-plan note may be the actual prompt, so the pair remains candidate-only.

I think we shall return about 15th or 16th
I have told my clerk to send to your house the charts on Coral reefs you kindly lent me

The Lyell extract on glacier theory is missing.

issues: All 23 assigned packet records were read in full: every retained body paragraph, each header, metadata audit, editorial summary, and editorial footnote was reviewed.
All cited body quotations were recursively checked as exact substrings of the cited packet paragraph and all paragraph coverage arrays enumerate every retained body paragraph.

Incoming Lyell text is never treated as Darwin voice. The 425 link to 424 is a supported reverse reply and the 604→602 link remains candidate-only; neither establishes when Darwin received or read the incoming letter.

DCP-LETT-421F remains explicitly held: it is an ambiguous bounded public petition with multiple signatories, not eligible private correspondence. Its original XML hold and attribution constraints are preserved.

DCP-LETT-425 has distinct 6 and 8 September sections; DCP-LETT-376 has 29 August and 5 September sections; DCP-LETT-649 has 5 and 7 October sections; DCP-LETT-590, 592, 605 and 653 retain bounded or date-uncertain ranges; DCP-LETT-696 retains the 15-or-22 September alternatives. No section was backdated from a later paragraph.

The candidate 480→425 shell-information link is deliberately candidate-only. The exact intervening Lyell note and any oral discussion would be needed to promote it. The 604→602 change-of-plan context likewise needs the missing later note before promotion.

External records needed include the missing Lyell query behind 394, the forwarded letter behind 602, the extracts/manuscripts behind 590, 592, 594 and 595, and the unlocated items listed above. Topic overlap, catalogue adjacency and publication references were not used as proof.
